title: Dinner at Grandpa's (a 4-person family scene, written for experiments E8 and E10)
lines: Tom, have you finished your homework yet?
Almost, Mom. I just need to finish the last question.
Good. Dinner will be ready in ten minutes.
Grandpa, will you tell me a story tonight?
Of course, sweetheart. Which one do you want to hear?
The one about the dragon and the little boat!
Ah, I told you that one last week. Don't you remember the ending?
I remember, but I want to hear it again.
Amy, you always ask for the same story.
So what? You always play the same game.
That's different. My game has new levels every week.
Amy, please put the spoons on the table.
Okay, Mom. How many spoons do we need?
Four, one for each of us.
Linda, do you need any help in the kitchen?
No thanks, Dad. Please just sit down and rest.
I have been resting all day. Let me at least cut the bread.
All right, but be careful with that knife.
Grandpa, did you really sail across the sea when you were young?
I did. I was about your age when I first left home.
Very scared. But my father said that brave people are scared too.
See? Even Grandpa was scared. You're scared of spiders!
I am not! I just don't like them.
Tom, wash your hands before you sit down.
Thank you. Now help your grandpa with the bread.
Grandpa, give me the knife. I'll do it.
Thank you, my boy. Cut them thin, the way your mother likes.
Grandpa, after dinner, the dragon story. You promised!
I promised, and I always keep my promises.
Dad, you spoil her too much.
That is what grandfathers are for.
Mom, can Tom listen to the story too?
Only if he finishes his homework first.
I'll finish it right after dinner, I promise.
You have to sit next to me then.
Fine, but no kicking under the blanket.
Tom, you used to kick too when you were little.
Really? I don't remember that at all.
Of course you don't. You were only five.
Dinner is ready. Dad, please sit at the head of the table.
